title: Notifications docs
intro: Notifications sends WhatsApp, e-mail, SMS, browser push, staff push and webhooks for your website, through your own provider keys. Other products send through it with the Notifications server token pasted into their Connections; your own server sends with the same API. Your website's tokens are in the Portal: open the website, then Install and tokens. The browser token is public and goes into your pages; the server token is secret and stays on your server.
localhost: Testing on your own computer: the browser token also works on pages served from localhost, *.localhost, 127.0.0.1 or [::1], on any port, over http or https. These pages use your website's real database, keys and providers, so what you send there is sent for real. There is no test mode.
send: Send a message with the server token: POST /v1/messages/<channel> (email, sms, whatsapp, push or staff-push) with the template key, the recipient and the values. The answer (201) is the message as the delivery log keeps it: status sent, queued (waiting for its time), retrying, failed or skipped (unsubscribed or over a send limit). Send an Idempotency-Key header so a repeated request is refused instead of sent twice. Name the values that must never be kept, such as a code or a sign-in link, in secretValues (for example ["code", "link"]): the message is sent with them, and the delivery log keeps them hidden (****** or [link hidden]).
templates: Templates live in Notifications: one per template key, channel and language, written in the product dashboard (Settings → Templates) or in the template editor widget. Write {name} where a value goes, and {?name}…{/name} around text that shows only when the value name is not empty (for example {?tracking}Track it: {tracking}{/tracking}); sections may hold other sections of other names. A WhatsApp template with a template name at Meta (providerTemplate) may list buttons, [{ index, type, value }]: index is the button's place in the template at Meta (0–9), type is copy_code or url, and value may hold placeholders, for example {code}. A copy-code button copies its value (it is sent as Meta's authentication templates take it, as a url button whose text is the code); a URL button adds its value to the end of its address. Template keys of other products' own events start with the product id (accounts., ecommerce., chat., payments., growth.) and work while the channel is on; every other key is yours and needs the Merchant send API feature. Your server reads and changes templates with the server token: GET /v1/templates (the templates of switched-on channels), PUT /v1/templates (one template, with the same checks as the dashboard) and DELETE /v1/templates/<key>/<channel>/<language> (default for the default version); each channel's templates need its feature on, and writes count in the settings API's 60 writes per minute. Each change shows in Recent changes with the acting user of the SS-Actor-* headers, else Server. A sensitive template keeps none of its values in the delivery log (they show as ****** or [link hidden]); the templates of Accounts (accounts.…: sign-in codes, magic, reset and setup links) always are. A required message (sign-in codes, order and account updates) is always sent; any other message is optional and is not sent to people who unsubscribed. Optional messages can use {unsubscribeUrl}; e-mails also get one-click unsubscribe headers. An urgent message ignores quiet hours.
retries: A message that fails is tried again on the same channel, on the next uses of your website after each wait (there are no background jobs, so on a quiet site it waits for the next request). The Retries setting of e-mail, SMS and WhatsApp picks the plan: short (3 attempts: now, then 1 and 5 minutes later; the default) or long (6 attempts: now, then 5 and 15 minutes and 1, 3 and 6 hours later). Push messages use the short plan, and a message keeps the plan it was sent with. Then, with the Fallback channel feature, it is sent once on the fallback channel set in Settings (for example WhatsApp, then SMS) when the recipient has that address and a template exists for it. Every attempt is in the delivery log, kept forever in your own database.
timing: Quiet hours hold messages that are not urgent until the end of the quiet window in the recipient's time zone (to.timeZone, else the time zone in business.json). Send limits skip messages over the hourly or daily cap per recipient. Delayed send takes sendAt (ISO-8601); the message goes out on the first use of your website after that time, so it can be late on a quiet site.
languages: With Multi-language templates on, a template can have a version per language. The recipient's language (language, else to.language) picks the version: the exact code, then its base language (pt for pt-BR), else the default version.
providers: Connect a provider per channel in the product dashboard (Connections). E-mail: SMTP, Resend, SendGrid, Mailgun or Amazon SES. SMS: Twilio, or any gateway over HTTP. WhatsApp: Meta WhatsApp Cloud API, Twilio, or any gateway over HTTP (for example Connectivity.pk). A gateway over HTTP takes the address, json or form, optional headers as a JSON object and a body template where {to}, {toDigits}, {text} and {secret} are filled. Example for Connectivity.pk: address https://connectivity.pk/api/messages/chat, form, body instance_id=<your instance>&token={secret}&to={toDigits}&body={text}&priority=0.
keywords: Unsubscribe keywords: point your provider's incoming-message webhook at the address below. Twilio requests are checked with your auth token; the WhatsApp Cloud API with the app secret (and the verify token for its first check). A reply that is one of the keywords in Settings unsubscribes that number from optional messages.
push: Browser push: create a P-256 key pair (VAPID, for example with npx web-push generate-vapid-keys) and enter it in Connections → Push keys. Copy the service worker below to the root of your website as /ss-notifications-sw.js, then place the push-permission widget. When a visitor turns notifications on, the widget fires the ss-notifications:subscribed event on window with { subscriberId } and keeps it in localStorage; send it to your server and link it to your user, then send with to: { subscriberId }. Staff push works the same way in your admin with a ticket (permission push.subscribe); send with to: { staffId } (the user id in the ticket).
webhooks: Outgoing webhooks: add up to 5 https URLs in Settings → Webhook URLs, each with the events it takes (none: every event), and a random signing secret (at least 24 characters) in Connections. Your server reads and saves the same list with the server token: GET /v1/lists/webhook_urls and PUT /v1/lists/webhook_urls with { value: [{ url, events }] }, where events lists full types such as message.failed or payments.payment.paid. Each event is a POST of JSON { id, type, createdAt, websiteId, data } with the header SS-Signature: t=<unix seconds>,v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of "<t>.<body>">. Check it before trusting the body, and refuse times older than 5 minutes. A failed delivery is retried up to 5 times on later uses.
events: Other products' events: with the Notifications server token pasted into their Connections, every product that publishes events (for example payments.payment.paid) forwards each one right after it happens to POST /v1/events with { id, type, at, data } and the event id as its Idempotency-Key. Those events go to the webhook URLs that take their type (or take every event), signed the same way; the Events setting picks among Notifications' own events only. The webhook keeps the product's event id as id and its time as createdAt, so your server can match it with that product's GET /v1/events. id (evt_…) and at (ISO-8601) are optional: without them the webhook gets a new id and the time it was received.
log: The delivery log is kept forever in your own database. It never keeps a secret: the values of sensitive templates and those named in secretValues are hidden in its words and values, also in data-rights exports. Your server reads it with GET /v1/messages?status=&channel=&to=&cursor=&limit= (newest first) and GET /v1/messages/<id>, and counts it with the same filters: GET /v1/messages/count → { count, capped } and GET /v1/messages/counts?by=status|channel|template|source → { total, groups } (a one-off message from your staff counts under template none). The delivery-log widget reads the same with a ticket (log.read) under /v1/admin/messages.
install: Add the script to the pages of your website and place the visitor widget where it should appear. Widgets render nothing while their feature is off or the product is stopped.
admin: Admin widgets run in your own admin with a ticket: the delivery log (log.read), the template editor (templates.edit), send a message (messages.send) and staff notifications (push.subscribe). Include the script without data-token, place the widgets and register your ticket function. The widget calls it at start and 1 minute before the ticket expires; your server checks the user's sign-in and role every time.
tickets: Your server asks for a ticket with the server token (never send the server token to a browser). The origin is the address of your admin page: any https origin, or a local one while testing. Tickets last 15 minutes and carry only the permissions of switched-on features.
business: Every product reads your business basics from https://<your domain>/.well-known/business.json. Only name is required; without the file the name is your domain and the time zone is UTC.
api: Every route answers JSON; errors are RFC 9457 problems with a stable code. Lists are paged with cursor and limit. Routes of a feature that is off answer 403 feature_off.
